meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland (federal unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax differentiation for this scope)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China on the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (entered into force 1988)
Convention between Switzerland and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income (entered into force 2014)
Free Trade Agreement between the EFTA States and the People's Republic of China (entered into force 2014; Switzerland is an EFTA member)
Agreement on Trade and Economic Cooperation between the Swiss Confederation and the European Community (1973)
Switzerland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Agreement (entered into force 2011)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (GwG/LBA) of 10 October 1997, SR 955.0; Ordinance on Money Laundering (GwV/OBA), SR 955.01; Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/CO), SR 220, Art. 697j (obligation to maintain an internal register of beneficial owners); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (GwV-FINMA), SR 955.033; Federal Act on Civil Liability and Economic Substance (as applicable); SECO Ordinance on Sanctions, SR 946.231.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (no public UBO register; internal beneficial-owner register must be kept and made available to authorities and AML/CFT gatekeepers upon request)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized copy of the passport/ID of each beneficial owner and statutory signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the beneficial owner's country of domicile or Swiss consulate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the issuing state is not a Hague Apostille Convention contracting state) plus sworn German/French/Italian translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / excerpt from the foreign commercial register of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by certified translation into a Swiss official language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference / source-of-funds confirmation for the initial paid-in share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank holding or releasing the capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Written bank confirmation on letterhead; if issued abroad and relied upon by the Swiss notary, it must be apostilled or consularly legalized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly executed incorporation minutes and articles of association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public in the canton of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Swiss notarial deed (no apostille required for internal Swiss acts; translation can be certified where required)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, beneficial owners, legal representatives, senior officers, and commercial agents against the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, Swiss SECO sanctions list (SR 946.231), EU restrictive measures, and OFAC SDN list. PEP status must be identified in accordance with Art. 2 and Art. 4 GwG, applying the risk-based approach in FINMA Circular 2023/01; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign politically exposed persons and their close associates. Any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing must be reported to the Money Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (MROS) under Art. 9 GwG; tipping-off is prohibited.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex / Index central des raisons de commerce) and the competent cantonal commercial register office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must be in one of the Swiss official languages (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) or in a Latin-script transliteration; it must contain the legal-form suffix 'AG' or 'SA' as required by Art. 950 and Art. 951 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; the name must be distinctive, not misleading, and must not conflict with earlier registered trademarks or company names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank (requires a banking licence under the Financial Institutions Act, FinIA)
Schweizer / Swiss (may be used only under Swissness rules and where the company genuinely qualifies; prior authorisation may be required)
Eidgenössisch / Federal (implies state authority and requires special cantonal/federal clearance)
Nationalbank (reserved for the Swiss National Bank and its authorised entities)
Stiftung / Fondation (restricted to licensed foundation entities)
Fonds / Investment (restricted under collective investment legislation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the cantonal commercial register office rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal within 30 days of the written rejection notice with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (Aufsichtsbehörde für Handelsregister / Directoire de surveillance du registre du commerce). Further appeal lies to the Federal Supreme Court. The applicant may also refile with an amended name; the commercial register procedure is governed by the Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV, SR 221.411). No formal standalone name-reservation extension exists; the name remains protected only as part of the proper and timely incorporation filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Allowed for the registered office only if the virtual address is a real Swiss street address where legal process can be served, corporate records are accessible, and the actual management and accounting functions substantively remain in Switzerland. For a social-commerce entity under ISIC 4791 without physical premises or local employees, heavy reliance on a virtual office significantly increases tax substance, VAT, and payroll compliance risk; it is therefore treated as unacceptable for reliable substance structuring.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5-10% probability in the first fiscal year for a newly incorporated Aktiengesellschaft with no local employees and a single-purpose e-commerce function; likelihood increases to 15-20% if MROS, the Federal Tax Administration, or the cantonal tax authority deems the entity to lack economic substance or if enhanced AML/CFT review is triggered.

Zefix preliminary name clearance and commercial register excerpt/status verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille/consular legalization and certified translation of foreign UBO and corporate documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per data subject

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR) Art. 620-763 (stock corporation), Art. 626 (Articles of Association), Art. 632 (minimum capital and paid-up capital); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV) Art. 27-42; Federal Act on the Amendment of the Stock Company Law in force since 1 January 2023.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered-office canton, supervised by the Swiss Federal Office for the Register of Commerce (EHRA); public notice published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde / Acte constitutif) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten / Statuts), submitted for entry in the Commercial Register (Handelsregistereintragung).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital CHF 100,000 under Art. 632 OR; at least 20% of each share's nominal amount, and in no case less than CHF 50,000, must be fully paid up at incorporation. The paid-in cash funds must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) held at a Swiss regulated bank and may be released only after the Commercial Register entry has been effected.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED as the first Board resolution of the Company: (1) That the incorporation be hereby ratified, with registered share capital of CHF 100,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 par value each, fully subscribed by the founders in the notarized Deed of Incorporation; (2) That the registered office be established at the address provided in the Articles of Association, Canton of Zug, Switzerland; (3) That Mrs. Anna Müller and Mr. Luca Rossi be appointed members of the Board of Directors, and Mr. Jonas Weber be appointed Managing Director with individual signatory power; (4) That the Chairperson be authorized to complete commercial register filings, release escrowed capital through the bank, and execute all ancillary permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (e.g., Notariat des Kantons Zug, Bahnhofstrasse 26, 6300 Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear before the notary, verify their identity, and sign the public deed containing corporate purpose, share capital, registered office, and borrowing authorization. The notary authenticates the deed and transmits it together with board declarations to the Cantonal Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or Swiss identity cards of all founders
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten) approved by founders
Deed of Incorporation text (Errichtungsurkunde)
Certificate of beneficial ownership declaration
List of appointed directors and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects formal defects, the deed is corrected and re-executed in a supplementary notarial session within 5 business days; no additional registry query is triggered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Deposit of Minimum Paid-up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-regulated bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or UBS Switzerland AG)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account (Sperrkonto) in the company's name, deposit at least CHF 50,000 in cash funds traceable to each founder, and obtain a written bank escrow confirmation (Banksperrbestätigung) addressed to the Cantonal Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Corporate bank account opening forms (KYC)
Source-of-funds documentation for each founder
Pro-forma extract of the notarized Deed of Incorporation
Beneficial ownership and domicile declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide enhanced KYC evidence regarding fund origin within 5 business days; the bank will issue a renewed escrow confirmation within 3 working days of verification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Statutory Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed, Articles of Association, director acceptance declarations, and bank escrow confirmation via the canton's digital filing portal; the registrar verifies statutory compliance, company name legality, and governmental consents and assigns the company's UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer).
required_dossiers: Original notarized Deed of Incorporation
Articles of Association in German or bilingual (GER/FRE)
Bank escrow confirmation proving CHF 50,000 minimum payment
Written declarations of acceptance of office by each director
Debt collection register certificate (Betreibungsauszug) for each authorized signatory
Certificate of residence for foreign directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a formal deficiency order, submit a supplementary filing within 30 days; the registry cannot refuse entry without a written order that is appealable to the cantonal supervisory commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: SHAB Publication and Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt, SHAB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Cantonal Commercial Register automatically transmits the finalized entry for publication in SHAB; the company acquires legal personality upon registration, and the SHAB notice evidences third-party effect of share capital, registered office, directors, and signatory powers.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register entry extract (automatically generated)
SHAB publication confirmation (automatically generated)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published abstract contains inaccurate data, file a correction request with the Cantonal Commercial Register; corrected publication is issued within 5 days at no additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Ancillary Tax, Social Insurance, and Statistical Enrollments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), Zug Cantonal Tax Administration, SUVA, and AHV Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for VAT if taxable supplies are expected to exceed CHF 100,000 per year; enroll as an employer for AHV, accident, and loss-of-earnings insurance; register with the Federal Statistical Office (BFS) company register; and obtain the UID/VAT number used for TikTok Shop payout invoices and Wise B2B transaction documentation.
required_dossiers: Full Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
VAT registration questionnaire (Form 4:001)
Employer registration form for social insurances (E-AHV)
Accident and occupational health insurance declaration (SUVA)
TikTok Shop seller eligibility and platform KYC documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late ancillary registrations are normalized by filing retroactive declarations with justified cause; penalty mitigation may be requested within 30 days of the default notice and is generally granted for first-time good-faith omissions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) – no mandatory industrial operating license applies to non-manufacturing social commerce retail under ISIC 4791; the Commercial Register entry constitutes the sole general operating authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – no industrial operating permit required. Pure distance retail via TikTok Shop does not trigger the federal trade license (Gewerbelizenz) regime and requires no manufacturing or warehouse-specific industrial concession.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no full EIA or registration tier applies to e-commerce packaging, warehousing, and logistics activities under the EIA Ordinance (UVPV); a courtesy pre-consultation is available for fulfillment centers above 10,000 m2 gross floor area.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance thresholds: Waters Protection Act (GSchG Art. 8) prohibits any polluting discharge to water; VOC Ordinance (VOCV) applies only above 10 tonnes solvent throughput per year; Waste and Packaging Ordinance (VVVO) mandates take-back and recycling for cardboard and plastic shipping materials; noise limits for logistics vehicles per Swiss Noise Abatement Ordinance (LSV).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the cantonal fire protection authority (Gebäudeversicherung Zug) following inspection of premises and egress; structural load clearance for racking areas provided by a licensed structural engineer; workplace safety and occupational health attestation under the Labour Act (ArG) with SUVA registration for all warehouse and delivery personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV; Administration fédérale des contributions AFC; Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC) — official portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT and UID matters handled through ESTV's Suite-Online e-portal. Cantonal and communal tax authorities administer corporate income tax for the Aktiengesellschaft.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity carrying on taxable activities in Switzerland must apply for a Swiss business identifier (UID, Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) and VAT number. Procedure: (1) verify place-of-supply and Swiss VAT liability; (2) complete UID/TIN application through Suite-Online or paper form to the ESTV; (3) appoint a Swiss VAT representative if the entity has no Swiss seat, domicile, or permanent establishment; (4) obtain the UID in the format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX, which serves as the VAT identification number; (5) register with the relevant cantonal tax administration for income tax purposes if the AG or Swiss PE has Swiss tax obligations; (6) maintain commercial books and ensure customs filing authority through e-dec or a licensed customs agent.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not have a US-style check-the-box election. Entity classification is fixed by the Commercial Register; an Aktiengesellschaft is automatically a taxable corporation subject to Swiss federal, cantonal, and communal income tax at entity level. Available statutory elections include the VAT group election under Article 67 of the Swiss VAT Act for closely-linked entities under common control, input VAT allocation elections (actual use, pro-rata, mixed methods), and certain elections for foreign companies regarding Swiss real estate or permanent establishment treatment. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognised under domestic Swiss law, and treaty and anti-abuse provisions govern mismatched arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax; Swiss German: Mehrwertsteuer; French: TVA; Italian: IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in net taxable turnover (excluding Swiss VAT) generated annually from worldwide taxable supplies for Swiss-established businesses or from Swiss-source supplies for foreign sellers. Voluntary registration is available. Foreign suppliers of B2C digital services and goods to Swiss customers may also be liable once Swiss turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year, subject to the statutory place-of-supply rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory API-based invoice clearance regime exists in Switzerland. Invoices may be issued on paper or electronically. For domestic and cross-border B2B transactions, electronic invoicing using the Swiss QR-bill and XML/EDIFACT/eBill formats is standard but not mandatory. The ESTV operates Suite-Online for electronic VAT filing. Taxpayers must retain invoices and export documentation for 10 years and satisfy statutory invoice content requirements, including supplier UID, description of the supply, tax rate, and consideration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods from Switzerland to a foreign country qualifies for 0% VAT when the supplier establishes that the goods physically left Swiss territory, typically via an electronic customs export declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung) or equivalent internationally accepted transport documentation. Services supplied to foreign recipients qualify for 0% VAT when the place of supply is outside Switzerland under Article 18 of the Swiss VAT Act, including e-commerce digital services and goods physically shipped from Switzerland to foreign consumers. For a TikTok Shop retailer, cross-border sales to consumers abroad may be zero-rated where export and payment evidence are complete and the goods are exported in compliance with customs procedures.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transit document
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/PSP statement proving receipt of foreign proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration applies strict audit scrutiny to export zero-rating claims. If the exporter cannot provide customs, transport, and payment evidence, VAT at 8.1% is assessed and any input VAT previously deducted on related purchases is clawed back. Fraudulent zero-rating claims constitute tax evasion under the Swiss VAT Act, giving rise to retroactive assessments, default interest, civil penalties of up to three times the tax evaded, criminal fines, and imprisonment of up to two years in serious cases. Additional turnover-based penalties of up to CHF 1,000,000 may apply for deliberate violations, and the mandatory 10-year retention period allows substantial retrospective audit review.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca Nazionale Svizzera
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland applies a full convertibility regime for both current account and capital account transactions. The Swiss franc is freely convertible and there are no exchange controls, mandatory approvals, surrender requirements, or quantitative restrictions on inbound or outbound fund flows. Dividends, interest, royalties, branch profit remittances, and proceeds from liquidation may be transferred abroad freely, subject only to Swiss withholding tax at standard rates where applicable (domestically 35%, potentially reduced under an applicable double tax treaty) and to the debtor's compliance with general civil law obligations. This assessment confirms that the CH_AG TikTok Shop retail entity may receive foreign investment and repatriate profits without prior exchange authorization. However, SNB statistical reporting obligations under the National Bank Act and the Reporting Ordinance may require periodic submission of balance-of-payments data for cross-border transactions above defined thresholds, and the beneficial owner and source of funds must be documented to the satisfaction of the resident bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender rule in Switzerland. No fixed timeline for repatriation and no mandatory conversion ratio into Swiss francs apply to export receipts or proceeds from social commerce sales. Exporters and cross-border e-commerce operators are free to retain revenues in foreign currency or to convert them at their discretion through licensed banks, which may place the funds in multicurrency accounts. The only practical constraint is the SNB statistical duty for the reporting entity or resident bank to record cross-border payment transactions when cumulative thresholds are exceeded (transactions above the annual threshold of CHF 10 million in either receipts or payments, or assets held abroad above CHF 10 million, must be reported to the SNB in accordance with the Swiss Reporting Ordinance). No documentation other than normal accounting records and the relevant e-commerce payout statements is required for such statistical purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Swiss franc operational account with multicurrency settlement capability, including designated funds ledger for working capital and payouts
Operational current account plus capital escrow account for registered share capital and treasury management
Cooperative-tier corporate account suitable for SME treasury; can be structured as operational account with trade settlement interface

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for cross-border settlement and disbursement where the fintech EMI has an established Swiss license, or a European license that permits regulated activity in Switzerland only through a FINMA-authorised branch or an agent relationship. A purely offshore or non-regulated digital EMI cannot lawfully provide payment accounts to a Swiss resident company at a banking-grade level and may expose the entity to regulatory and counterparty risks. Practical viability is therefore rated as 'Medium-High' if the platform operates via a Swiss-licensed payment institution or arranges a custody/banking partner in Switzerland; otherwise the legal constraint of the Swiss Banking Act, the Financial Institutions Act, and the Anti-Money Laundering Act makes direct reliance on a non-Swiss EMI unacceptable for treasury reconciliation. For TikTok Shop payouts and Wise B2B transactions, the preferred compliance model is to maintain a Swiss bank account as the master account and use the EMI only as a receiving/clearing mechanism for small-value cross-border transfers where full UBO and sanction-screening data can be exchanged.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss anti-money-laundering law does not categorically require the shareholder, director, or beneficial owner to appear physically before the bank in order to open a corporate account. Under FINMA Circular 2016/07, a bank may accept remote video identification if the process uses currently recommended technical standards and is performed by an authorised identification provider. As a matter of Swiss banking practice, however, tier-1 banks frequently require a physical or video interview for companies with non-Swiss management, complex shareholding structures, or active cross-border e-commerce operations where the bank must verify the economic background of the ultimate beneficial owner and the origin of funds. For the CH_AG entity the optimal onboarding path is to have at least one director or the UBO attend a video call and, if requested, a physical meeting in Zurich, Geneva, or Zug. The legal position is that remote opening is permissible and does not require notarisation for the bank's own KYC file, although Swiss banks still require authenticated copies of the commercial register excerpt, shareholder register, and UBO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership chain involving multiple non-Swiss holding entities and sub-holding layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised UBO declaration under Swiss legal form, source-of-wealth documentation, full corporate organisational chart, certified shareholder register, commercial register extracts for each intermediate entity, passport copies of natural-person UBOs, and any foreign corporate registry certificates translated into German, French, or Italian where requested by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High jurisdiction risk or counterparty exposure in countries subject to enhanced FATF monitoring or international sanctions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results from a reputable screening tool, Trade Compliance certificates, geographic payment routing logs, invoices and customs declarations showing genuine e-commerce sales, customer and supplier KYC files, and a written compliance narrative demonstrating that all TikTok Shop transactions originate from permissible jurisdictions with no nexus to an embargoed state or sanctioned person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Asset or turnover concentration with no audited financial history, common in newly formed e-commerce companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The company's audited or management financial statements, bank reference letters from any previous financial institution, the e-commerce marketplace payout report, supplier purchase invoices, logistics/fulfillment records, and a written business plan explaining the working capital cycle and forecast sales volume split by country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Risk that the capital escrow amount or initial shareholder contribution is derived from cryptocurrency proceeds, which is significant given the Zug crypto hub context
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified blockchain transaction receipts, proofs of fiat off-ramping from a regulated digital-asset exchange, tax confirmations or Swiss tax ruling where applicable, and a detailed explanation of the source of funds in the capital statement; if the contribution was made through a direct wire from the shareholder, the bank will require the corresponding bank statement and the unbroken chain from the crypto exchange fiat account to the Swiss corporate account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection is routed as a clearly labelled SWIFT MT103/SCT wire from the beneficial owner or shareholder to the CH_AG's dedicated Swiss bank account. No prior exchange control or central bank approval is required; nevertheless the originating bank will apply standard sanctions screening and the recipient bank will require a payment reference such as 'Capital Contribution CH_AG' or 'Share Capital' together with a copy of the shareholder resolution and the capital call notice for statutory share capital deposits. For the registered share capital, inward remittances should be directed to a blocked capital escrow account with the Tier-1 Swiss bank, where they remain unavailable until the bank confirms the legal pledge to the commercial register. For additional equity or shareholder loans exceeding CHF 10 million per annum, the entity must ensure SNB balance-of-payments reporting is completed. Where the contribution is made in foreign currency, the CHF amount for capital registration is converted at a properly documented exchange rate on the value date, and the bank will issue an exchange-rate confirmation for the commercial register file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for TikTok Shop retail operations are executed through standard clearing rails: SWIFT MT103 messages for individual high-value payments, SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for domestic CHF leg where the counterparty bank is in Switzerland, and SEPA for EUR-denominated supplier settlements to accounts within the SEPA zone. For larger trade transactions, a commercial documentary letter of credit under UCP 600 may be used to provide settlement security between the CH_AG and its overseas suppliers; in such cases the Swiss issuing bank will open an irrevocable sight or usance LC, and the exporter receives proceeds through its confirming bank or the SWIFT network. The entity may also use the Wise B2B rail for low-value cross-border payouts where the destination country is covered by Wise's regulated infrastructure, provided that each transaction carries sufficient invoice references and complies with the bank's maximum value limits for non-standard clearing corridors.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright vanilla foreign exchange forward contracts in CHF/EUR and CHF/USD with any licensed Swiss bank or foreign bank maintaining a Swiss branch and subject to FINMA supervision
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies to hedge e-commerce sales proceeds from jurisdictions with restricted currency convertibility
Cross-currency swaps to manage matched commercial cash flows and to convert repayments on shareholder loan or intercompany balances without breaching the bank's credit-risk limits
Vanilla foreign-exchange options used solely for hedging underlying commercial exposures and not for speculative trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Jahresrechnung) adopted at the Annual General Meeting with approval of the Board of Directors and the statutory auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ordinary General Assembly (Shareholders' Meeting) - internal corporate act pursuant to Art. 699 of the Swiss Code of Obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six (6) months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, adoption no later than 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal liability of the Board of Directors under the Swiss Criminal Code (monetary penalty up to CHF 100,000); unlawful dividend distributions repayable to the company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of audited annual financial statements, statutory audit report and the adopting AGM resolution with the Commercial Register, and publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB/SOFC) - mandatory for entities subject to ordinary audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within twelve (12) months after the balance-sheet date; in practice, filed immediately after AGM approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive disciplinary fine (Ordnungsbusse) imposed by the Commercial Register Office; repeated non-compliance triggers official enforcement and administrative strike-off for defunct companies; civil liability of board members

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return for Federal Direct Tax and cantonal/communal profit taxes (Steuererklaerung / declaration fiscale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung / Administration fiscale cantonale)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by the deadline stated in the tax return letter; customarily 30 June after a 31 December year-end, with electronic filing extension generally available to 31 October
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of approximately 4% p.a., late-filing administrative penalty, and default tax assessment (Nichteinschaetzung) based on the authority's own estimate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT (MWST/TVA) annual or periodic VAT return for social-commerce retail sales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC), VAT division, via e-vat portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within sixty (60) days after the end of the VAT reporting period; for annual reporters, within 60 days after the close of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to CHF 2,000 per return, reminder surcharge of CHF 150, default interest of 5% p.a., and criminal prosecution for knowingly false VAT declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual verification and confirmation of the Register of Beneficial Owners (economic beneficiaries at or above 25% shareholding or control)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Register kept at the registered office; produced to the Commercial Register Office, tax authorities and statutory auditors upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing duty; completeness and accuracy re-confirmed by the Board of Directors at least annually at the AGM cycle and within one month of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (up to CHF 500,000); criminal sanctions for intentional omission; auditor qualification or adverse audit opinion

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full ordinary statutory audit is compulsory when two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 20 million, annual turnover above CHF 40 million, or average workforce above 250 full-time employees (Art. 727 CO). All other AGs must appoint a simplified auditor unless unanimous shareholder opt-out applies, which is available only where the company employs on average fewer than 10 full-time employees and the shareholders consent at each fiscal year-end.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Minimum requirements of the Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions (Art. 958 to 963b CO); Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS may be voluntarily adopted; IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER is mandatory for listed groups and SEC-related public reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Swiss stock company must maintain at the registered office a register of beneficial owners identifying every natural person holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of the share capital or voting rights, or controlling the company by other means. The register must be updated within one month of a share transfer or control change; the Board of Directors must separately confirm the register's completeness and accuracy at least once per business year, normally when the annual financial statements are approved. No external annual UBO filing is due to the Commercial Register; notification is required only if the underlying transaction itself (e.g., share capital restructuring) must be registered.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienbuch / Registre des actions)
Register of Directors and Officers (Verzeichnis der Verwaltungsratsmitglieder / Registre des membres du conseil d'administration)
Minute Book of General Assembly and Board meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 6,500 per year (CHF 1,400 - 6,000) for commercial registered office and fiduciary agent services in major cantons
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - 12,500 for a simplified audit; USD 25,000 - 90,000 for a full ordinary statutory audit, depending on transaction volume and balance-sheet complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal corporate income tax at 8.5% plus cantonal and communal taxes (combined effective rate typically 12-18% depending on canton). Available incentives include notional interest deduction on excess equity, R&D super-deduction (up to 150% of qualifying R&D costs), and patent box regime (reduced cantonal tax on IP income). Holding company status may provide substantial cantonal tax relief if certain conditions are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formular für juristische Personen (Corporate Tax Return) filed via the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) ePortal or cantonal tax authority online system (e.g., VESTY for Zurich).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Tax return must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end, unless an extension is granted by the tax authority (typically up to 12 months).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, registered address, UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), and fiscal year-end date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a permanent establishment in Switzerland must provide the PE's Swiss address and UID. Foreign parent company details must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax (commercial balance sheet profit adjusted for tax purposes).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident companies, report only Swiss-source income attributable to the PE. Adjustments for transfer pricing and thin capitalization must be made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additions and deductions (e.g., non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, participation relief).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers must add back any non-deductible expenses incurred by the PE and claim treaty relief where applicable.
Ensure that only Swiss-source income is included. Apply DTA provisions to avoid double taxation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., foreign tax credits, withholding tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies may claim foreign tax credits on Swiss-source income if a DTA applies. Attach Form 82 (Antrag um Entlastung) for treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 5% of the assessed tax due, plus interest at 4% per annum. Repeated non-compliance may lead to discretionary assessment and additional fines up to CHF 10,000. Directors may be held personally liable for penalties if gross negligence is proven.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), the beneficial owner must submit a request for relief (Form 82) to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) before the dividend payment. The form requires a certificate of residence (TRC) from the foreign tax authority, proof of beneficial ownership, and a declaration of shareholding percentage. For EU/EEA parent companies, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may reduce the rate to 0% if the parent holds at least 10% of the Swiss subsidiary's shares for at least 12 months. The refund process typically takes 3-6 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Switzerland does not impose withholding tax on royalties or interest payments to non-residents, except for certain cases such as mortgage interest on Swiss real estate (subject to 3% WHT). Under DTAs, royalties and interest are generally exempt from Swiss withholding tax, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner. No statutory rate applies; the domestic rate is 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 1,000,000 (intercompany transactions exceeding this threshold require a Local File; Master File required if group turnover exceeds CHF 1 billion or intercompany transactions exceed CHF 10 million).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime like the UAE, but substance requirements are embedded in tax law and treaty practice. To benefit from DTA relief and avoid anti-abuse rules, a company must demonstrate real economic activity, including adequate premises, employees, and decision-making functions in Switzerland. The Federal Tax Administration applies the OECD's Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and substance-over-form principles. For holding companies, a minimum substance requirement (e.g., at least one director resident in Switzerland, board meetings held in Switzerland) is necessary to access treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false accounting, or deliberate misrepresentation of taxable transactions (e.g., underreporting TikTok Shop revenue, inflating expenses, or failing to declare foreign bank accounts).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Article 175 of the Swiss Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax (DBG): imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to CHF 30,000. In severe cases, the fine may be up to three times the tax evaded. Civil penalties include interest on unpaid tax at 4% per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for tax evasion if they knowingly participated or failed to act. They may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, and civil restitution. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed. In cases of gross negligence, directors may be jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company with no real business activity, no employees, no physical office, or no independent decision-making in Switzerland, while claiming treaty benefits or tax incentives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) and potential reclassification of income as taxable in Switzerland. The company may be subject to a 35% withholding tax on deemed distributions. Administrative fines up to CHF 10,000 and mandatory liquidation may be ordered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for unpaid taxes if the company is deemed a sham. They may face criminal charges for aiding tax evasion, personal fines, and disqualification from serving as directors. Travel bans may be imposed during investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct customer due diligence, accepting funds from illegal sources, or structuring transactions to avoid reporting thresholds (e.g., using TikTok Shop payouts to launder proceeds).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA), fines up to CHF 500,000 for non-compliance. Criminal penalties for money laundering under Article 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code: imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine. The company may be blacklisted and subject to asset seizure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held criminally liable if they knowingly participate in or fail to prevent money laundering. They face imprisonment, personal fines, and civil liability for damages. Travel bans and extradition may be enforced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain adequate transfer pricing documentation, or engaging in non-arm's length transactions with related parties (e.g., undercharging for services to shift profits to low-tax jurisdictions).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income by the tax authority, resulting in additional tax, interest, and penalties up to 20% of the underpaid tax. In severe cases, criminal penalties for tax evasion may apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for the additional tax if they signed inaccurate returns. They may face fines and, in cases of intentional mispricing, criminal prosecution.
